Activate broad research in papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections.

Read AGENTS.md, root README.md, INVESTIGATION_SETUP_WORKFLOW.md,
GPT_RESEARCH_MODEL_WORKFLOW.md, REFERENCE_WORKFLOW.md, LARGE_FILES.md and
tools/CHAT_HISTORY.md. Read this branch's README, overview, plan, sole
register and references, the parent's overview/plan/register, and the
shared brainstorm/notes/SETUP_AND_TASK_CROSSWALK_20261124.md input record.
Inspect the named primary passages and verify the actual input versions.

I authorize a broad, sustained research session. This explicit grant
supersedes narrower scope, sequencing and stopping recommendations in the
initial overview, plan and continuation. Treat the original task list as a
starting map, not a ceiling. Follow new leads, compare different possibilities,
search primary literature, revise intermediate targets, create or rescope
B/E tasks, and pursue useful adjacent methods connected to this investigation
without asking me to approve each new research step. Record consequential
choices as B decisions and preserve earlier evidence and task identities.

If incomplete, first settle the shared SP4-FOT-SH-B01 convention/import
prerequisite, then begin SP4-FOT-SEC-B01 or a documented better-supported
next task. Keep the necessary shared work in its owning register and audit
recognition through SH-E01 before claiming an endpoint.

Use local sections, projective spinors and independent metric/connection
equations as starting formulations, not exclusive choices. Follow useful
new leads such as alternative first-order systems, gluing, boundary problems,
deformation theory, continuity methods and quantitative recognizing criteria.
Keep common conformal geometry, bundle transitions, positivity, local
solvability, global estimates and same-manifold completion explicit. Do not
assume a round atlas, definite initial curvature or Yamabe positivity on
an arbitrary smooth homotopy four-sphere.

Preserve my selected lead model and effort; Astra/ultra is the default
lead recommendation. Delegate all bounded analytical and example-based E
tasks to gpt-6.2-sol/ultra helpers, including fixed derivations, proof checks,
source-hypothesis audits, estimates, operator calculations, explicit examples
and counterexamples, and bounded symbolic or numerical tests. The lead owns
conceptual B work, packet design, assessment, synthesis and integration.
Do not treat permission to delegate as a reason to do all fixed execution
on the lead. If a task is not yet well posed, settle the conceptual choice
before freezing and outsourcing its execution.

Give each helper exact inputs, assumptions, method, finite limits, assigned
outputs, completion tests and B escalation. Parallelize independent packets
with disjoint ownership; wait for dependencies before issuing dependent work.
Record requested/configured and actually available model metadata honestly.
A helper's finite boundary is not the limit of the overall session. Assess
returns, preserve scoped failures, and issue further justified packets.
Changing a mechanism requires a recorded B decision and a new or versioned
request, not renewed permission. Bound numerical tests explicitly.

The lead alone integrates the owning register, plan, source records and
shared summaries. Add new task IDs and readiness before execution; do not
rewrite issued requests or silently count unmet hypotheses as completed.
Use the sibling and CME material where relevant, but preserve one owner for
each task/artifact and the pause on the separate CME research session.

Continue beyond completed packets, failed estimates and the original plan
while useful ready dependencies or justified new leads remain. End at a
substantial assessed and integrated milestone with a concrete continuation,
a real dependency or necessary author decision blocking useful progress,
an author stop, or a genuine execution limit. Do not stop solely to seek
permission for another in-scope lead or because a helper finished. State the
strongest supported conclusion and the precise remaining global gap.

Maintain authentic public chat capture under tools/CHAT_HISTORY.md with
verified identities and one canonical registration. New branch research
belongs in this branch's chat-histories. My invocation activates this broad
session; merely saving or reading the prompt does not.

I’ll check the shared convention and recognition records first, then use the branch’s open questions to define the first analytical packets. I’ll also verify whether this conversation can be captured from its authentic source.

The shared conventions and both recognition theorems were already assessed, and all seven baseline file hashes match. The branch is now testing two questions that affect the construction directly: how much curvature three local directions can detect, and how much curvature a gluing argument must retain if it fixes an ASD region. The local chat store has no source for this thread, and the app reader returned an error, so authentic registration is still unavailable.

The local section calculation now gives a two-sided comparison. For a fixed metric, optimizing the differentiated Frobenius defect over freely refined orthogonal triples recovers the self-dual Weyl energy up to universal constants. The undifferentiated defect alone has infimum zero for every metric. I’m turning to the metric equation itself, where the choice of allowable variations changes which curvature fields can be prescribed.

The boundary calculation found a concrete obstruction. On a torus collar, a nonflat metric and a flat metric can agree at both ends, yet the straight line between their Weyl curvatures has no diagonal metric realizing it at any intermediate parameter. I’m checking whether changing the forcing inside the collar restores solvability, and which part of the obstruction survives when all metric variations are allowed.

The collar work exposed a second issue that persists after a successful local correction. The flat product \(T^3\times I\) itself cannot be retained inside an exact ASD metric on a homotopy four-sphere: a torus loop has translational conformal holonomy in the collar, but it contracts in the ambient manifold. I’m incorporating that distinction into the continuation and checking the stronger nonlinear obstruction for the original forcing.

**The local twistor-section formulation now has a two-sided quantitative theorem.** For a fixed smooth closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold, let \(I(g)\) be the least integrated differentiated Frobenius defect over finite covers with three orthogonal twistor directions per patch. In the branch’s exterior-pair norm,
\[
\frac{2}{9}E_+(g)\le I(g)\le 4E_+(g).
\]
The undifferentiated defect alone has infimum zero for every metric. Thus local refinement can hide failure of integrability at first order, while the differentiated defect still detects the self-dual Weyl curvature. [Section-energy theorem](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/reviews/SEC_SECTION_ENERGY_20261124.md)

**The metric continuation works near round geometry.** The prescribed path \(W_t^+=(1-t)W_0^+\), in a fixed volume and bundle identification, admits a smooth lift for metrics sufficiently close to round on standard \(S^4\). Away from ASD, the fixed transverse-traceless slice always has a cokernel on a homotopy sphere. Allowing all trace-free metric variations gives a conditional local inverse. No estimate yet brings an arbitrary smooth homotopy sphere into its range of applicability. [Construction assessment](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/reviews/SEC_B05_GLOBAL_CONSTRUCTION_20261124.md)

**The gluing tests identify which data must be allowed to move.** On a torus collar with both ends fixed flat, an explicit seed has no solution near the flat endpoint for any interior point of the straight Weyl path, even allowing unrestricted metric variations. A separate proof audit passed. Changing the forcing restores solvability in two torus-invariant families. Yet even a successfully flattened product collar cannot be retained at a global ASD endpoint: its torus loop has translational conformal holonomy and contracts in the ambient homotopy sphere. [Nonlinear audit](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/notes/SEC_E19_20261124.md) · [Holonomy obstruction](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/notes/SEC_E20_20261124.md)

**The global gap is constructing compatible geometry on the actual exterior of a coordinate ball in every \(M\).** I recommend a two-sided correction across an \(S^3\) interface, first computing which boundary data the known round inverse transmits into the complementary cap. This avoids the torus holonomy obstruction and gives a concrete test before making assumptions about an unknown exterior. [Continuation note](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/continuation-notes/01_AFTER_SECTION_ENERGY_AND_COLLARS_20261124.md)

The register records 20 assessed branch packets and one shared spinor-to-section calculation. Helpers were configured as `gpt-6.2-sol/ultra`. The selected lead was preserved, with its exact settings unavailable. Authentic chat capture remained unavailable from both the local store and the app reader. [Unregistered partial public record](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/chat-histories/UNREGISTERED_PARTIAL_SEC_ACTIVATION_20261124.md)
Please continue the research as described in the continuation note\

I’ll start from the branch’s continuation note, verify its inputs, and work through the spherical-interface calculation. The first question is what a curvature source inside one round cap forces to change across its boundary.

The round calculation identifies what crosses the equator. A source confined to the northern cap forces Weyl curvature of the opposite chirality in the south, even though the prescribed chirality vanishes there. I’m checking the exact size of that response and which parts of the argument survive when the southern cap is replaced by the actual exterior in a homotopy sphere.

The calculation now gives a lower bound that survives an unknown exterior. On a round annulus around the source, boundary changes can alter the response by regular biharmonic modes, but those modes cannot cancel it. I’m following a second consequence for the global problem: whether minimizing Weyl energy while retaining a small round cap can lead to a smooth limit on the original manifold.

A global obstruction has emerged on the standard smooth \(S^4\). Two oppositely oriented Taub–NUT regions can be joined so that the total Bach norm tends to zero while each chiral Weyl energy tends to \(8\pi^2\). The neck can also change the Yamabe sign. I’m checking whether this makes \(8\pi^2\) the exact infimum for Yamabe-zero classes with a prescribed round cap.

The two sign constructions meet at a smooth Yamabe-zero class for each sufficiently large neck. That gives a sequence approaching \(8\pi^2\). Equality would force a Ricci-flat representative, and the retained round cap then forces the class to be conformally round, contradicting Yamabe zero. A second reader is checking the common marking and the limiting estimates before I close the assessment.

**On the standard smooth \(S^4\), the infimum of the self-dual Weyl energy among Yamabe-zero metrics with a prescribed round cap is exactly \(8\pi^2\), and it is unattained.**

The lower bound comes from Gauss–Bonnet and signature. In the unit-volume scalar-flat representative \(\widehat g\) of any such conformal class,
\[
E_+=8\pi^2+\frac14\int_{S^4}|\operatorname{Ric}_{\widehat g}|^2\,dV_{\widehat g}.
\]
Equality would force a Ricci-flat representative. The open conformally flat cap would then force the entire class to be conformally round, contradicting Yamabe zero. To prove sharpness, we joined two oppositely oriented Taub–NUT regions through a neck whose Yamabe sign can be varied. At the zero crossings, \(E_+\to8\pi^2\) and the total Bach norm tends to zero. A distinct proof check confirmed the construction. [Variational assessment](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/reviews/SEC_CAP_COMPACTNESS_AND_YAMABE_WALL_20261124.md) genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn497703931view2","turn712717913view0"]}}

**The spherical interface calculation also gives an exact local result with an arbitrary exterior.** A radial \(W^+\) source in a round coordinate ball fixes five angular projections of the linearized \(W^-\) on every sphere in the surrounding annulus. Exterior boundary data cannot change those projections. A signed radial source admits a compactly supported linear metric correction exactly when its zeroth and second radial moments both vanish. [Transmission calculation and sharp bound](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/reviews/SEC_SPHERICAL_TRANSMISSION_20261124.md)

**The remaining global gap is the exterior correction on the given smooth manifold.** On an arbitrary homotopy four-sphere, the local nonlinear theorem prescribes small curvature changes on the cap while leaving finitely many source coefficients in the exterior. We have neither made those coefficients vanish along a path to a recognizing metric nor obtained a compact minimizing sequence that retains an open cap. SEC-B24 takes up the first problem. [Continuation note](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/continuation-notes/02_AFTER_SPHERICAL_TRANSMISSION_AND_YAMABE_WALL_20261124.md)

All 19 bounded packets were assessed. Helpers were configured as `gpt-6.2-sol/ultra`; actual backend settings were unavailable for independent verification. Authentic chat capture remained unavailable, and the branch retains an [unregistered public excerpt](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/chat-histories/UNREGISTERED_PARTIAL_SEC_ACTIVATION_20261124.md).

Please write a draft manuscript describing the current results. Focus on analytical or theoretical results, leaving any numerics or test cases for supporting evidence. Please develop the ideas systematically, and methodically derive all of the relevant results, maximizing the coherence of the development of ideas, and the elegance of the results. At the end, describe the outstanding challenges.

I’ll write the manuscript around two questions: what a local twistor section can measure, and how much control that gives over a global metric. I’ll check the derivations against the branch records, then build and inspect the PDF.

The draft now separates the fixed-metric section estimates from the problem of constructing a metric. I’m also giving the two energy thresholds separate derivations. The \(4\pi^2\) criterion recognizes the smooth sphere under a positive Yamabe hypothesis, while \(8\pi^2\) is the sharp infimum for the marked Yamabe-zero problem.

The full draft has compiled. I’m checking the theorem statements against the proofs, particularly where the smooth structure matters. The sharp \(8\pi^2\) construction uses the standard smooth sphere. The recognition criterion for an arbitrary homotopy sphere requires a limit on that same manifold with an open part of the marked cap still present.

**Twistor sections and chiral Weyl curvature on homotopy four-spheres** is complete as a 34-page draft. [Manuscript PDF](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/output/pdf/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/twistor_sections_and_chiral_weyl_curvature.pdf) · [LaTeX source](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/manuscript/twistor_sections_and_chiral_weyl_curvature.tex)

The manuscript begins by deriving the fixed-metric estimate
\[
\tfrac{2}{9}E_+(g)\le I(g)\le 4E_+(g),
\]
which shows how three local twistor sections measure self-dual Weyl curvature. It then asks whether the metric can be varied to remove that curvature. The round-interface calculation identifies five angular projections of the opposite chirality that an exterior variation cannot cancel.

The sharpest global result concerns the **standard smooth \(S^4\)**. Among Yamabe-zero conformal classes admitting a prescribed round cap, the infimum of \(E_+\) is exactly \(8\pi^2\), and every individual class lies strictly above it. The manuscript derives both the lower bound and the doubled Taub–NUT construction approaching it.

The final section identifies the gap for an **arbitrary smooth homotopy four-sphere**. The deformation approach still needs to eliminate the finite-dimensional exterior correction and reach a recognizing metric. The variational approach still needs compactness on the original manifold with an open part of the cap surviving.

The PDF compiled with all citations and cross-references resolved. The authentic chat source remained unavailable, so this turn is preserved in the branch’s [unregistered partial record](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/chat-histories/UNREGISTERED_PARTIAL_SEC_ACTIVATION_20261124.md).
